title: Down time
goals: Talk about what you do (and don't do) in your free time using the simple present.
Ask and answer yes/no questions and questions with What, Where, When, Why and Who.
Ask for an opinion and respond naturally (What do you think? How about you?).
Describe your personality and other people's using adjectives (shy, funny, sociable…).
Understand and write short texts about likes, hobbies and daily routine.

learn.title: Simple present: affirmative, negative and Yes/No questions
learn.html:
Used to talk about likes, habits and routines (what you normally do). With I, you, we, they the verb does not change; with he, she, it we add -s (or -es / -ies). To make negatives and questions we use the helper do / does, and the main verb goes back to its base form. Careful: with action verbs, do/does is used instead of be; don't mix them.

AffirmativeNegativeQuestionShort answer
I / you / we / they listen to music.I / you / we / they don't (do not) listen.Do you / they listen to music?Yes, I / they do. / No, I / they don't.
He / she / it listens to music.He / she / it doesn't (does not) listen.Does he / she listen to music?Yes, he / she does. / No, he / she doesn't.

Spelling of the third person: most verbs only add -s (plays, buys); verbs ending in -ch, -sh, -s, -x, -o add -es (watches, goes); consonant + y changes to -ies (studies). With a particle: wakes up, works out.

watch.why: With does, the verb is in the base form.
With doesn't, the verb is in the base form.

watch.wrong: Does he read books? Yes, he reads.
watch.why: The short answer uses do/does, not the verb.
With action verbs, use do/does, not be.

learn.title: Simple present: information questions
learn.html:
Used to ask for specific information: when, where, who, what, why. The question word goes first, then do / does, the subject, and the verb in its base form.

WordStructureExampleTypical answer
WhatWhat + do/does + subject + verb?What does Lisa do in her free time?She plays tennis.
WhereWhere + do/does + subject + verb?Where does Carmen play tennis?In the park.
WhenWhen + do/does + subject + verb?When do Bob and Jerry go bowling?On the weekend.
Who (with whom)Who + do/does + subject + verb + with?Who does Linda play tennis with?Her sister.
WhyWhy + do/does + subject + verb?Why does Lisa like tennis?Because it's relaxing.

Why is answered with because. In Who … with? the preposition goes at the end.

watch.wrong: What he does in his free time?
watch.right: What does he do in his free time?
watch.why: The helper goes before the subject.

watch.wrong: Why does Richard stays in that job?
watch.right: Why does Richard stay in that job?
watch.why: With does, the verb has no -s.
does is only used with he/she/it.

learn.title: Strategy: asking for opinions
learn.html:
Used to invite the other person to talk and keep the conversation going.

QuestionWhen to use itPossible answer
What do you think?After giving your opinion.I'm not sure. They're OK sometimes.
How about you?To give the question back.I don't play sports.
What's your opinion?More formal or direct.I prefer hip-hop.
Do you agree?To check if they think the same.Yes, I do. / No, I don't.

learn.title: Useful expressions
learn.html:
• Can I ask you some questions for a survey? — to start a short survey or interview.
  • Sure! Go ahead. — to say yes and let the person start.
  • Thanks a lot! / Sure, no problem. — to say thank you and reply to thanks.
  • I'm not sure. — when you don't have a clear opinion.
  • I prefer … — to say what you prefer.
  • I'm very / quite … (shy, sociable…) — describing your personality.
  • I like / enjoy going / playing … — talking about your hobbies.
  • I really like … / I love … — to show a strong like.
  • Because it's relaxing, healthy and fun. — giving reasons with because.
  • They're always there for me. — talking about a loyal friend.

reading.title: My weekends with friends
paragraphs: Hi Emma! You ask about my free time and my friends, so here is some news. I'm quite sociable, and I love weekends. On Saturdays, I go bowling with my friends Rafa and Lupe. Rafa is very funny. He tells jokes all night! Lupe is shy, but she is a loyal friend.

On Sundays, I don't go to parties. I listen to music and I practice the guitar at home. My brother Beto doesn't play the guitar. He plays video games and goes online. He is an introvert, so he doesn't like big groups.
What do you do in your free time? Do you like sports? Where do you meet your friends? What do you think about bowling? Write soon! Paola
